sources.entry: Collaborative software or groupware is designed to help people working on a common task to attain their goals. Groupware often regroups multiple services such as file sharing, calendar/events management, appointment scheduling, address books... in a single, integrated application.

summary.name: Collaborative software
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia overview of collaborative software (groupware), application software that helps people working on a common task reach their goals.
use_cases: understanding categories of team collaboration software
comparing real-time editing with version control
organizing team calendars and project schedules
summary.what_it_does: This Wikipedia article describes collaborative software (groupware) as a broad category of application software for people working on a shared task. It distinguishes real-time collaborative editing of a single file from version control, which keeps parallel edits as variant files. It groups collaborative management tools such as document collaboration systems, electronic calendars, project management systems, workflow systems, and online spreadsheets. The page also covers the history from Engelbart's 1960s work through early systems like Lotus Notes, plus design issues such as persistence, authentication, and concurrency.
notable: Traces groupware history from Engelbart's 1968 demo to Lotus Notes and early military systems
Splits collaboration into communication, conferencing, and coordination levels
Covers design challenges like persistence, authentication, and concurrency
caveats: Encyclopedia article, not a software product; it names no specific tool to download or buy
Some sections are flagged by Wikipedia editors as essay-like or lacking citations
